# Oxford English Dictionary

> > The definitive historical dictionary of the English language, documenting word meanings, etymology, pronunciation, and usage from Old English to the present day.

The Oxford English Dictionary (OED) is the authoritative scholarly resource for English lexicography, providing comprehensive entries with etymological analysis, historical citations from sources like William Prynne and Roger Ascham, frequency data, and detailed documentation of obsolete, archaic, and contemporary words across all varieties of English including Latin borrowings, loanwords from languages like Javanese, and regional dialects.

## Key Topics

- Etymology
- Historical linguistics
- Lexicography
- Latin borrowings
- Obsolete and archaic words
- Word frequency data
- Pronunciation guides
- Middle English
- Old English
- 16th-century English
- Historical citations
- Word formation and morphology
- Loanwords and language contact
- Regional and dialectal variation
- Semantic change

## Dictionary Entries: Core Words and Prefixes

- [a-, prefix¹ meanings, etymology and more](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/a_prefix1): Morphological and etymological analysis of the a- prefix
- [a-, prefix³ meanings, etymology and more](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/a_prefix3): Old English word formation analysis of the a- prefix
- [abide, n. meanings, etymology and more](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/abide_n): Obsolete Middle English/Scottish noun with historical usage
- [aberrate, v. meanings, etymology and more](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/aberrate_v): Verb with Latin etymology and historical citations
- [abdominous, adj. meanings, etymology and more](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/abdominous_adj): Adjective with Latin origin and usage examples

## Latin Borrowings and Classical Derivations

- [abbreviature, n. meanings, etymology and more](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/abbreviature_n): Obsolete Latin borrowing with historical documentation
- [ablactation, n. meanings, etymology and more](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/ablactation_n): Middle English Latin borrowing with medical usage
- [abannation, n. meanings, etymology and more](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/abannation_n): 18th-century obsolete Latin borrowing
- [abhorration, n. meanings, etymology and more](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/abhorration_n): Historical noun with Latin roots

## Loanwords and Foreign Language Borrowings

- [abangan, n. meanings, etymology and more](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/abangan_n): Javanese loanword with detailed etymology
- [abanderado, n. meanings, etymology and more](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/abanderado_n): 16th-century Spanish military loanword
- [abas, n. meanings, etymology and more](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/abas_n): French loanword cited by John Phillips

## Ecclesiastical and Religious Terms

- [abbot-presbyter, n. meanings, etymology and more](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/abbot-presbyter_n): Ecclesiastical term with historical church usage
- [Aaronid, n. & adj. meanings, etymology and more](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/aaronid_n): Proper noun derivative from Biblical Aaron

## Historical and Archaic Compound Words

- [abbey-lubber, n. meanings, etymology and more](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/abbey-lubber_n): 16th-century archaic compound word with historical context
- [abdominal belt, n. meanings, etymology and more](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/abdominal-belt_n): Noun with historical usage and frequency data

## Abbreviations and Initialisms

- [ABD, n. meanings, etymology and more](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/abd_n): North American academic initialism (All But Dissertation)
- [A.B., n. meanings, etymology and more](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/ab_n-d): US English abbreviation with AAVE usage

- [abearance, n. meanings, etymology and more](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/abearance_n): Obsolete word cited by Roger Ascham
- [abigailship, n. meanings, etymology and more](https://www.oed.com/dictionary/abigailship_n): Obsolete 1840s word by Jane Porter
